purpose: Bound the novelty claim while evaluating source-guided constructive search; this is a literature comparison, not an implementation or experimental result.

source.title: Trace-Guided Synthesis of Effectful Test Generators
source.scope: PLDI is a programming-languages venue; it is relevant related work, not an ICSE/ISSTA acceptance claim.

paper_mechanism: Clouseau uses supplied operation specifications with symbolic effect histories. Its synthesis refines abstract traces by adding dependencies required by an operation, then derives test generators. The paper's introductory put/get example already connects operations through a shared key. See sections 1, 2.1 and 4.1, Algorithms 1 and 2.

not_novel_by_itself: Joining read and write operations using a common key
Guiding test sequence synthesis with dependencies
Starting from an observation and constructing preceding operations
comparison.current_local_prototype: Extracts limited MAY read/write address terms from available candidate code, then unifies a source donor action with an existing test observation. It neither implements Clouseau's type system nor obtains its guarantees.
comparison.unresolved_research_question: Can automatically recovered constraints from existing agent validation code produce useful unseen combinations cheaply, while keeping intended oracle semantics independent of the potentially faulty candidate implementation?
comparison.required_evidence: A new candidate or a source-address match is insufficient. Compare equal source pools and budgets, actual useful combinations, correctly justified failing tests, false alarms, and cost. Separate automatic source extraction from any manually supplied semantic specification.

experimental_effect: No frozen candidate-generation protocol, provider budget, or prior result changed because of this literature lookup.
